claim: a condensed technique that LOCATES the non-trivial zeta zeros without zetazero: sign-changes of the real Riemann-Siegel Z function (Gabcke remainder), each zero found by bisection; re-derives the decimal-perspective statistics from the roots it finds

setup.engine: Riemann-Siegel formula: main term 2*sum_{n<=N} cos(theta - t ln n)/sqrt(n), N = floor(sqrt(t/2pi)); Gabcke remainder C0..C4 (5x44 coefficients, 50 decimals, from terry98004/libHGT, MIT); theta exact via log Gamma

zeros_found.note: sign changes of the real Z function bracket every simple zero; all of the first 100 zeros are simple

decimal_perspective_reproduced.note: the decimal-perspective verdict is unchanged when the zeros come from this engine instead of zetazero

condensation.note: the main sum's cutoff floor(sqrt(t/2pi)) is the condensation: at most 6 terms evaluate Z anywhere in the first-100-zero search, while the naive Euler-Maclaurin/Dirichlet count grows as t (the repo already measured that route failing on the critical line for t >= ~30); per evaluation at t_100 this is a 6.3x condensation vs the t/2pi count

verdict: RIEMANN-SIEGEL ROOT ENGINE VALIDATED: engine: Z(t) matches |zeta(1/2+it)| to rel 5.2e-05 on the critical line; roots: the first 100 zeros located by sign-change + bisection on the Riemann-Siegel Z function, max |t_RS - t_mpmath| = 3.1e-06 (mean 9.5e-08), WITHOUT zetazero; decimal perspective reproduced from the RS-found zeros: <r>=0.6108 (GUE 0.5996, z=+0.58, KS p=0.6842), residual std 0.225 (-3.02 sigma below uniform decimals), RvM S-residual max 0.9979 < 1 within log(t)/pi = 1.74 - the same verdict as riemann_decimal_perspective.py, now from roots the engine itself found; condensation: the main sum uses floor(sqrt(t/2pi)) terms, never more than 6 in this run (t_100=236.52) - the window grew by sqrt(4.1) while t grew 16.7x, and per evaluation that is 6.3x fewer main terms than the t/2pi Euler-Maclaurin count at the last zero; NOT a test of RH (100 zeros cannot probe RH - the Riemann-von Mangoldt residual is a measurement of the count residual, within its O(log t) bound, not a claim about the hypothesis).
